elements.evidence: Section 9.4 expressly permits Customer to terminate the Agreement or any Order Form for convenience.

elements.element: Customer's termination for convenience may be exercised on thirty days' prior written notice.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 requires thirty days' prior written notice to Vendor.

elements.element: Upon Customer's termination for convenience, Vendor must refund prepaid Fees covering the period after the effective date of termination.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 requires Vendor to refund all prepaid Fees covering the post-termination period.

elements.element: The refund of prepaid Fees must be calculated on a pro-rata basis.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 expressly states that the refund will be made on a pro-rata basis.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 expressly prohibits Vendor from terminating the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience during a committed term.
Section 9.4 expressly grants Customer a termination-for-convenience right.

elements.element: Customer's termination for convenience requires 60–90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 requires only thirty days' notice, which is outside the specified 60–90-day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer must not exceed three months' Fees.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause imposes no early-termination fee, so the conditional cap is not exceeded.

elements.element: Any Vendor termination for convenience may take effect only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 prohibits Vendor termination for convenience during a committed term, thereby preventing it from taking effect before the term ends.

elements.element: Any Vendor termination for convenience requires ninety days' notice.
elements.evidence: No operative language imposes a ninety-day notice requirement on any Vendor termination for convenience.

result.reason: The redline fully implements the preferred position: Customer receives a convenience right on thirty days' prior written notice, the required pro-rata refund applies, and Vendor is barred from convenience termination during a committed term. The fallback is not independently satisfied because its 60–90-day Customer notice period and ninety-day Vendor notice requirement are absent. The change is substantively focused and preserves the existing breach, insolvency, and Order Form termination provisions, although placing Section 9.4 after Section 10.2 is a minor organizational defect.
